rows.source: ORR level-crossing risk management
rows.verified: ORR identifies level crossings as a priority risk area where the public interacts directly with the railway.

rows.source: ORR level-crossing risk management
rows.verified: Primary responsibility for managing level-crossing risk rests with infrastructure managers working with train operators, local and highway authorities and users.

rows.source: ORR level-crossing risk management
rows.verified: Risk changes with train frequency, speed and noise, road traffic, larger farm machinery and distraction from electronic devices.

rows.source: ORR level-crossing risk management
rows.verified: ORR expects high-quality risk assessments by competent people who understand crossing hazards, controls and user behaviour and risk perception.

rows.source: ORR level-crossing risk management
rows.verified: ORR targets higher-risk passive footpath, user-worked and automatic half-barrier crossings.

rows.source: ORR level-crossing risk management
rows.verified: Closure should be considered first where reasonably practicable, while alternatives and improved protection must be explored if closure is not practicable.

rows.source: ORR level-crossing risk management
rows.verified: Risk should be reassessed when traffic, user profiles, train services or local land use changes, and after incidents, near misses or unsafe behaviour.

rows.source: ORR level-crossing risk management
rows.verified: Dutyholders should identify and assess risk, use competent reviewers, implement practicable controls and keep crossing layout, barriers, lights, alarms and signs under review.

rows.source: ORR level-crossing risk management
rows.verified: Level-crossing risk depends on crossing type, train and road traffic, user profile, sighting, warning and protection systems, maintenance and changing local conditions.

rows.source: ORR level-crossing risk management
rows.verified: ORR crossing evidence is route-, crossing-, train-, road-user-, control-, maintenance- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level collision probability.

rows.source: Environment Agency flood alerts and preparation
rows.verified: England uses three warning levels: flood alert means possible, flood warning means expected, and severe flood warning means danger to life and major community disruption.

rows.source: Environment Agency flood alerts and preparation
rows.verified: Flood risk should be checked even away from rivers or the sea, and warnings can be received by phone, text or email.

rows.source: Environment Agency flood alerts and preparation
rows.verified: A flood alert means prepare now; actions include readying the flood plan, insurance documents and medication, avoiding flood water and moving livestock and equipment.

rows.source: Environment Agency flood alerts and preparation
rows.verified: A flood warning means act now; people should move loved ones, pets and valuables to safety, use higher ground, isolate utilities if safe and follow emergency services.

rows.source: Environment Agency flood alerts and preparation
rows.verified: A severe flood warning means danger to life; people should stay safe, prepare to evacuate and call 999 if in immediate danger.

rows.source: Environment Agency flood alerts and preparation
rows.verified: A personal flood plan should cover valuables, measures to limit water ingress, insurance, evacuation and arrangements for pets.

rows.source: Environment Agency flood alerts and preparation
rows.verified: Flood warnings can be delivered by phone, email or text, and mass-alert messages should include practical preparation, response and support information.

rows.source: Environment Agency flood alerts and preparation
rows.verified: Preparedness should include targeted communication for vulnerable communities and a grab bag containing medication and insurance documents.

rows.source: Environment Agency flood alerts and preparation
rows.verified: Flood harm depends on the flood source, forecast, terrain, drainage, property, warning lead time, vulnerability, available support and response.

rows.source: Environment Agency flood alerts and preparation
rows.verified: Environment Agency flood evidence is forecast-, location-, property-, population-, response- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level harm probability.
